To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
family systems are linked to child symptoms and that this relation is moderated by the age of the child.

(a) family cohesion and adaptabililty are significantly correlated, but the relation is weaker for adolescents than for young children, (b) family systems and symptoms are negatively related, and (c) family systems and self-esteem are negatively related.

(1) the family system has a strong impact on children's behavior problems, (2) the family system is related to the child's self esteem, (3) the child's self- esteem moderates the family system-behavior problem relationship, (4) the child's sex moderates the family-system-behavior problem relation, and (5) the child's age moderates the family-behavior problem and self-esteem relationships.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relation between the family system, as assessed by the FACES III, and the symptomatology of the children.
the relations between family cohesion/ adaptability (i.e., family systems) and childhood behavior problems (e.g., symptoms of psychopathology).
the relations of family systems, self-esteem, and childhood symptomatology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
family cohesion and adaptabilty are related to the presence of childhood behavior problems.
family systems and symptoms are interrelated in complex ways, with self-esteem playing a mediating role in some instances and an independent role in others.

the relation between family functioning and child psychopathology depends upon the age of the child, the type of psychopathology being assessed, the method of assessment, the sample, and the theoretical framework being used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
family systems variables, such as cohesion and adaptability are related to child symptomatology and self-esteem, but these relations are not direct and are mediated by other factors.
family cohesion and adaptablility are related to the child's self esteem, which is related to the child having fewer symptoms.
families with children with behavior problems tend to be more enmeshed and rigid than families with children without behavior problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relation between family systems variables and children's symptoms is moderated by the child's age.
the family system is an important source of support and stress for children.
families that are more balanced are more likely to have kids who have fewer symptoms and are more likely to be self-assured.
